guide.summary: Each customer instance needs a registered OAuth application, and the user authorization code flow yields a bearer token acting as the connected person. The api_v3 scope covers the standard API, so work package reads are bounded by that user's own permissions.

findings.title: Authorization code flow obtains a user-delegated bearer token
findings.detail: The authorization code flow redirects the user to consent, then exchanges the code for an access token and refresh token that act on behalf of the current user. The access token expires after two hours by default and must be refreshed or re-requested.
findings.appliesWhen: The connected person authorizes the app and the app calls the API as that person.

evidence.quote: Authorization code flow example

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
The response contains the bearer token (“access_token”) and a refresh token that you will need when working with the API. Please copy the tokens for reference.

findings.title: api_v3 scope for the standard OpenProject API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is assumed when no scope is checked. It is a broad read/write API token, so the app must restrict itself to read-only calls; application restrictions do not make the token read-only. Access is further limited by the connected user's own permissions.
findings.appliesWhen: The application is registered with the api_v3 scope for work package reads on each customer instance.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.

findings.title: Each customer instance needs an OAuth application registration
findings.detail: An administrator adds an OAuth application under Administration, Authentication, OAuth applications, choosing a redirect URL and scopes, and records the client ID and secret for the app. Registration and token exchange are setup requirements, not resource actions.
findings.appliesWhen: Every customer organization or workspace connects its own OpenProject instance.

steps.title: Register OAuth application on the customer OpenProject instance
steps.detail: Customer admin signs in to the customer's OpenProject instance, opens Administration, Authentication, OAuth applications, clicks the green + OAuth application button, enters a name and redirect URL, selects the api_v3 scope, chooses confidential or public per the chosen client type, and saves. The client ID and client secret are then recorded securely. Expected output: a new OAuth application with a client ID; no secret is shown later.
steps.doneWhen: The OAuth application exists on the test instance and its client ID and secret are stored for the test.

steps.title: Open consent redirect and verify callback code
steps.detail: In a browser, open the documented authorization URL on the customer instance with response_type=code, the client ID, redirect URI, scope api_v3 and prompt=consent. The connected user signs in and approves. The browser is redirected to the redirect URI containing a code parameter; copy that code. Expected output: a callback URL carrying a code parameter.
steps.doneWhen: A callback URL with a code parameter is captured from the browser after user approval.

evidence.quote: https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
Typically the server that was requested with that redirect will save the authorization code and use it to obtain API token, with which the server can then act on behalf
In this example we skip that server side implementation and just copy the value of the code parameter from the URL that you see in your browser.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash
CLIENT_ID: from the registered OAuth application
REDIRECT_URI: the redirect URL configured on the application

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for bearer token
steps.detail: Exchange the code from the callback for a bearer access token and refresh token using the documented token endpoint with grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, the code, and the redirect URI. Expected output: JSON with access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 7200, refresh_token and scope api_v3.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains access_token, token_type Bearer and scope api_v3.

steps.title: Read first page of accessible work package titles
steps.detail: Call the work packages collection with offset=1, a chosen pageSize, and filters=[] so no default filter is applied. Titles are in each element's subject property under _embedded.elements. Expected output: a collection with total, count and _embedded.elements, where each element's subject is the title.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains _embedded.elements with subject values and total/count metadata. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
